newsitem.title: FRANCE: Hooded Corsican guerrillas claim bombing.
newsitem.headline: Hooded Corsican guerrillas claim bombing.

text.p: Hooded Corsican guerrillas have claimed responsibility for a bomb attack on the French Mediterranean island hours before a court sentenced a separatist leader to jail, a newspaper said on Saturday.

The daily Corse-Matin published photographs of five black-clad guerrillas of the "Historic Wing" of the Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) at a rare news briefing and said they claimed responsibility for the blast on Wednesday in the town of Bastia.
The bomb damaged law courts hours before a Bastia court sentenced Francois Santoni, leader of the political wing of the FLNC, in his absence to four months in jail for carrying guns.

A bomb exploded just after midnight on Saturday, wrecking a car owned by the bursar of a school at l'Ile Rousse, a Corsican town of which Veterans Affairs Minister Pierre Pasquini is mayor, police said.

No one was hurt by the explosion, and no one claimed responsibility. Corsica has been racked by hundreds of bombings in a two-decade-long separatist campaign for greater autonomy from mainland France.
Corse Matin quoted an FLNC spokesman at Thursday night's briefing, attended by three reporters, as saying: "The Corsican problem will not be solved except by peaceful means, not by arms."
The remarks were more conciliatory than recent threats.

On Friday, Prime Minister Alain Juppe vowed anew to apply the law in Corsica after the FLNC warned him against any attempt to "physically eliminate" its members, saying its response would be of an "incalculable violence".
